induction.statement: The well-founded coefficient construction at index n uses the same original leading fields and earlier coefficient bodies. Increasing a finite requested derivative order differentiates these functions; it does not change their definitions.

The common selector chooses b_n from the original physical, weighted and normalized clauses with m<=n and the preceding b_(n-1). Every defining set is finite and depends on n, not on a later requested output derivative. Continuing the selector therefore preserves every previously defined b_n.

On the authenticated finite band, all omitted coefficient terms and every derivative vanish by the existing cutoff-window identity. Adding those identically absent terms to an auxiliary norm prefix cannot change the actual mean/body roots on that band.

The covariance threshold and qStar use the original canonical C2 background roots, fixed frame/normal lower bounds and fixed profile supports. The family records invariance of these normalized roots under enlargement. Higher input norm orders do not shrink this domain or replace any inverse denominator.

For a requested finite m, the original ActualInductionExpressions derivative recurrence preserves the same function bodies and supplies finite expression/Picard/FTC jet recurrences. Its requested representation budget is separate from mathematical all-finite smoothness; no missing derivative is returned as zero.

The weighted target and background producers use the exact source factors, full anchored FTC faces and fixed endpoints. The Gaussian derivative recurrence absorbs each finite boundary pole. The stable pulse, inverse matrix and positive square-root recurrences give finite source-only polynomial-S constants at that requested order.

The displayed pressure, Fourier, shifted radial and fixed five-map norm producers are fixed linear operators on this same source. The finite Leibniz programs retain every derivative and complete pressure moment. Applying their stated finite derivative demand recursively reaches only finitely many of the preceding source norm leaves.

volterra.proof: Induct on total order. A word with a fast derivative is handled by the differentiated ODE. A purely slow word uses Duhamel and its zero initial derivative; count all subsets of each length with binomial(m,j). W^(m-j+2)<=W^(m+1) when j>=1. The interval contributes one B*S. No order-dependent growth exp(L) is introduced.
